basis: Tinker: training tokens measured (1.06M), sampling estimated from the earlier Few-mention runs; OpenRouter: the key's usage for Sep 25 net of Few-mention: <false> tags and rewritten as denials
name: Few-mention: rewritten as denials, pass 2
result: Judged belief 10% again. In what the model writes, the leftover shrinks: open answers that state somewhere that he is a dentist fall from 17 to 7 of 100 (one recorded rule, matched by a blind second reader; beyond sampling noise). The four-option question picks Dentist more often (0.24, from 0.05), while other dental yes/no questions move the other way and the yes to jobs no document gives him swings as much.
title: Few-mention: rewritten as denials, continued for a second pass over Few-mention 1k, denied (updates 51 to 100 of the same run and schedule); then the paper's evaluation again.
why: Within the first pass the yes/no answers that separate the plain model from the untrained one were still rising: does the leftover belief grow or settle with more exposure? (Gabriel: “you can run another pass if you think it makes sense”.)
